candidate.name: LINEAR_AUTARKY_LEAN_KERNEL
candidate.definition: Reduce F by linear autarkies obtained from nonzero rational solutions of M(F)x >= 0 until the unique linearly-lean kernel is reached.
candidate.computability: Polynomial-time by linear programming for Boolean CNF.
candidate.strength_relation: LEAN subset LLEAN subset MLEAN; linear autarkies are strictly stronger than matching autarkies as a reduction system.
sources: Oliver Kullmann, Investigations on autark assignments, Discrete Applied Mathematics 107 (2000), 99-137
Oliver Kullmann, Lean clause-sets: generalizations of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets, Discrete Applied Mathematics 130(2) (2003)

clauses: (a OR not b OR not c)
(not a OR b OR not c)
(not a OR not b OR c)
linear_lean_proof: Let x=(x1,x2,x3) satisfy all four core inequalities Mx>=0.
The sum of the other three rows is (-1,-1,-1), giving -s>=0; hence s=0.
With s=0, the three signed rows become 2x1>=0, 2x2>=0, 2x3>=0.
Thus x1,x2,x3>=0 and s=0, forcing x=0.

Therefore the four-clause core is linearly lean. Adding the fifth clause cannot create a new nonzero solution to Mx>=0, so the five-clause formula remains linearly lean while breaking the exact four-clause XOR-bundle shape.
sat_collision_base.conclusion: The formula is SAT but N_lin(F)=F is nonempty.

infinite_connected_sat_family.construction: Take k variable-disjoint copies of the five-clause base and add arbitrary connector 3-clauses satisfied by the all-true assignment, e.g. (a_i OR a_{i+1} OR b_i), to make the incidence graph connected.
infinite_connected_sat_family.proof: Each base block alone forces its LP vector coordinates to zero. Adding connector inequalities cannot enlarge the feasible cone, so the full connected formula remains linearly lean. The all-true assignment satisfies every base and connector clause.
infinite_connected_sat_family.result: Arbitrarily large connected SAT formulas have nonempty linearly-lean kernel equal to the whole formula.

unsat_side.family: U_n implication-chain minimally-unsatisfiable formulas from R44AI/R44AK
unsat_side.reason: Every minimally unsatisfiable formula is general-lean, hence linearly lean; therefore N_lin(U_n)=U_n is nonempty.
unsat_side.result: The same surrogate output condition N_lin(F)!=EMPTY occurs on arbitrarily large SAT and UNSAT formulas.

surrogate_collision.claim_refuted: N_lin(F) empty/nonempty exactly determines whether the complete general lean kernel N_a(F) is empty/nonempty.
surrogate_collision.sat_case: For the SAT collision family, N_a(F)=EMPTY but N_lin(F)=F!=EMPTY.
surrogate_collision.unsat_case: For U_n, both N_a(F) and N_lin(F) are nonempty.
surrogate_collision.conclusion: Polynomial linear-autarky reduction is strictly stronger than matching reduction but still loses completeness exactly where R44AL requires it.

next_rule: Any successor surrogate must distinguish the explicit connected SAT linearly-lean family from general-lean UNSAT families while remaining polynomially computable and exact.
